Both L- and D-HGNRs show CD peaks at the same wavelengths, 585 nm and 790 nm[1]. Their CD responses are mirror images of each other. The paper gives the g-factors as (cid:0) 0.0151 and 0.0150[2], "respectively". The PDF doesn't show which character comes before the first value. It is most likely a minus sign.

The sentence doesn't make clear what "respectively" refers to. It could mean the L and D forms, or the peaks. The g-factor plot ([3]Fig. 1[4], panel d) points to the first reading: L-HGNRs have a minimum of about −0.015[5] near the shorter-wavelength band, and D-HGNRs have a maximum of about 0.015[6] there. So L-HGNRs probably carry the negative value and D-HGNRs the positive value, both near the shorter-wavelength peak. That pairing is my inference from the plot, not something the text states.
